title: Slow-Roasted Chicken Breast with Lemon Pan Sauce
summary: Bone-in, skin-on chicken breast roasted low at 275°F to 155°F, seared for crisp skin, then served with a quick pan sauce of shallot, garlic, stock, lemon, butter and parsley.
notes: 49-second Short, 'Juiciest Chicken Breasts Ever', on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw); auto-generated captions only. The video gives no amounts and we found no written recipe, so every amount is our estimate: two bone-in, skin-on breast halves (USDA edible weight, meat and skin, 290 g for the pair), 1 tsp kosher salt, 1 Tbsp oil (some stays in the pan), 1 shallot, 2 garlic cloves, 1/2 cup stock, 1 Tbsp lemon juice, 1 Tbsp butter, 1 Tbsp parsley. Servings (2) and times (about 45 minutes at 275°F, plus searing) are estimates.

steps.text: Season the bone-in, skin-on breasts with salt and set them on a wire rack over a sheet tray.
Roast at 275°F until the thickest part reads 155°F (carryover brings it to 165°F). Rest 5 minutes.
Heat a film of oil in a pan over medium-high and sear the chicken skin side down about 2 minutes, then the other side and the edges. Rest again.
In the same pan, cook the shallot and garlic briefly, deglaze with the stock and lemon juice and reduce. Off the heat, swirl in the butter and parsley.
Slice the chicken and serve it with the pan sauce.
